boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented IU Bloomington rituals, recurring events, songs, and visual traditions—from a bronze handshake for exam luck to a bicycle race dating to 1951.

cards.title: Race in the Little 500
cards.subtitle: IU’s student bicycle race, held since 1951
cards.notes: Watch the women’s and men’s races, then follow team exchanges and strategy around Bill Armstrong Stadium’s cinder track.
cards.short_summary: Student cyclists turn relay exchanges and 200 laps into IU’s signature spring spectacle.
cards.evidence_claim: IU Bloomington states that the Little 500 began as a student bicycle race in 1951 and remains an established campus tradition.
cards.source_title: Campus traditions at Indiana University Bloomington
cards.access_notes: Spectator admission and participant eligibility are event-specific; consult the current Little 500 schedule before attending.

cards.title: Shake Herman B Wells’s Hand
cards.subtitle: The bronze handshake associated with exam luck
cards.notes: Find the seated Wells statue in the Old Crescent, shake its extended hand, and frame a photo that shows the polished bronze.
cards.short_summary: A handshake with IU’s former chancellor has become a pre-exam ritual passed between students.
cards.evidence_claim: IU Bloomington’s official bucket list identifies shaking the hand of the Herman B Wells statue as a campus tradition.
cards.access_notes: The statue is outdoors; approach from the public campus walkway and avoid climbing on the sculpture.

cards.title: Watch the Light Totem from the Ground
cards.subtitle: Feet up against the Eskenazi Museum wall
cards.notes: After dark, settle beside the museum wall and watch Rob Shakespeare’s Light Totem cast changing colors across the exterior.
cards.short_summary: Students trade a gallery bench for the pavement while colored light moves across the museum façade.
cards.evidence_claim: IU Bloomington’s official bucket list directs students to lie on the ground and watch the changing lights on the IU Eskenazi Museum of Art.
cards.access_notes: View from an open exterior area without blocking entrances or paths; nighttime display conditions may vary.

cards.title: Meet at Rose Well House at Midnight
cards.subtitle: A romantic Old Crescent ritual
cards.notes: Choose a clear night, meet someone special beneath the limestone arches, and photograph the illuminated pavilion respectfully.
cards.short_summary: The small limestone pavilion becomes the setting for a distinctly IU midnight rendezvous.
cards.evidence_claim: IU Bloomington’s official bucket list includes sharing a moment with someone special in the Rose Well House at midnight.
cards.access_notes: Use lit public walkways, go with a companion, respect consent, and follow any posted campus access restrictions.

cards.title: Make the Indiana Promise
cards.subtitle: IU’s shared pledge of responsibility and respect
cards.notes: Read the pledge closely, make it during your IU welcome experience, and revisit its commitments when campus choices get complicated.
cards.short_summary: New Hoosiers voice a compact pledge linking academic ethics, accountability, and respect.
cards.evidence_claim: IU Bloomington describes the Indiana Promise as a commitment students make to the university, themselves, and one another.
cards.access_notes: The pledge text is publicly available online; ceremonial participation may be limited to incoming-student programming.

cards.title: Learn “Indiana, Our Indiana”
cards.subtitle: The student-written fight song first performed in 1912
cards.notes: Learn the refrain before a major campus gathering, then join the crowd when the band cues IU’s century-old fight song.
cards.short_summary: A 1912 student composition still supplies the words Hoosiers sing at major campus moments.
cards.evidence_claim: IU Bloomington states that the student-written fight song “Indiana, Our Indiana” began in 1912 and is sung at major campus occasions.
cards.source_title: Campus traditions at Indiana University Bloomington
cards.access_notes: The song is commonly performed at university and athletics events; admission rules depend on the host event.

cards.title: Line the Route for the Homecoming Parade
cards.subtitle: Floats and Hoosier spirit through campus
cards.notes: Check the annual route, arrive before the first float, and photograph student groups and crimson pageantry from the sidewalk.
cards.short_summary: Students and alumni turn the Homecoming route into a moving display of campus organizations and school color.
cards.evidence_claim: IU Bloomington identifies the Homecoming parade as part of its recurring Homecoming tradition for students and alumni.
cards.source_title: Campus traditions at Indiana University Bloomington
cards.access_notes: The route and date change by year; use the current official Homecoming schedule and remain in designated spectator areas.

cards.title: Stay on Your Feet for IUDM
cards.subtitle: A 36-hour student fundraiser honoring Ryan White
cards.notes: Apply through an official dancer team or committee, learn the event’s mission, and prepare for games, speakers, and performances.
cards.short_summary: A year of student fundraising culminates in 36 hours on foot for Riley Hospital families and pediatric research.
cards.evidence_claim: IU’s student-organization page says IUDM was founded in 1991 and concludes with a 36-hour event where more than 2,500 students stay on their feet.
cards.access_notes: Participation requires an official IUDM role or invitation; use the organization’s current application and event guidance.

cards.title: Spot the Candy-Striped Warm-Ups
cards.subtitle: Crimson-and-white stripes adopted by basketball in 1971–72
cards.notes: At an IU basketball event, look for the striped warm-up pants and photograph the pattern before play begins, when permitted.
cards.short_summary: A poolside visibility solution became the unmistakable warm-up pattern of Indiana basketball.
cards.evidence_claim: Indiana Athletics documents that IU basketball adopted candy-striped warm-ups in 1971–72 after the design originated with IU swimming and diving.
cards.access_notes: The warm-ups are visible at applicable athletics events; tickets, photography rules, and team apparel vary by event.

cards.title: Enter IU at New Student Induction
cards.subtitle: The formal welcome for incoming Hoosiers
cards.notes: Attend with your incoming class, listen for the ceremonial welcome, and take the Indiana Promise when prompted by university leaders.
cards.short_summary: An incoming class formally joins the IU community through a named ceremony and shared pledge.
cards.evidence_claim: IU Bloomington lists the New Student Induction Ceremony as a signature Hoosier Welcome event and describes it as students’ official welcome to IU.
cards.access_notes: The ceremony is intended for incoming students; follow the current Hoosier Welcome schedule and entry instructions.
